title: Intermediate Outside clause for module extension by zero stalk maps
statement: For a ringed space X, open W, module sheaf G on the localized opens of W, and x outside W, the stalk at x of the module sheafification of the direct-sum extension-by-zero presheaf of G is the zero module over O_X,x.

proof.text: Proof: Represent an arbitrary stalk element of the extension presheaf by a germ over V containing x. No inclusion V -> W exists, since it would imply x belongs to W. The direct sum indexed by these inclusions is therefore subsingleton, so the representative and its germ are zero. Thus the abelian presheaf stalk is zero. Mathlib's stalkFunctor_map_unit_toSheafify_isIso identifies it with the abelian stalk of the module sheafification: the underlying abelian sheafification is definitionally the same construction. Transport subsingletonness across this isomorphism and apply ModuleCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton. Source: Stacks Project, Sheaves Lemma 00A7 (3), via Lemma 00A5 and Lemma 007Z.

mathlib_searches.verdict: No full match; sheafification stalk lemma is used for outside. Restriction of schemes is insufficient for arbitrary ringed spaces.

mathlib_searches.query: The stalk of sheafification of a presheaf of modules is unchanged and extension by zero has zero stalk outside the open subset

For a sheaf of modules on an open subset, extension by zero has zero stalks outside the open and the unit is an isomorphism on stalks inside; transitions between nested opens are compatible with counits
